claims.text: Replit's Agent 3, OpenAI's Codex web agent, and long-running automation at Cursor are stated to run on Temporal.

Durable execution journals every workflow step (LLM call, tool invocation, external API request) before it runs and records the result when it returns; after a crash the next worker replays the journal to reconstruct state up to the last completed step.

Four guarantees named for durable execution: persistence of state across crashes, exactly-once execution of side-effects, suspend/resume across arbitrary delays without holding a running thread, and deterministic replay.

A checkpointer (e.g. LangGraph's PostgresSaver, DynamoDBSaver, Redis checkpointer) is not durable execution: the developer still owns retry, resume and side-effect deduplication, whereas durable execution makes the runtime own them.

The recommended architecture keeps the ReAct-style outer loop deterministic in workflow code and pushes every LLM call, tool execution and external HTTP request into an Activity/Step whose result is recorded on first run and looked up on replay.

Workflow code cannot read the system clock directly (use workflow.now()), cannot generate random numbers directly (use workflow.uuid4()), and cannot rely on changing global state; anything non-deterministic belongs in an Activity.
Andreessen Horowitz led a $300M Series D into Temporal on the AI agent thesis; AWS Durable Functions, Cloudflare Workflows GA and the Vercel Workflow DevKit launched around the same time.
Temporal raised $300M at a $5B valuation on February 17, 2026, with 9.1 trillion lifetime action executions on its cloud, 1.86 trillion from AI-native companies.

Temporal's notable customers listed are OpenAI, Snap, Netflix and JPMorgan Chase; Temporal integrated with the OpenAI Agents SDK in September 2025, and Pydantic AI ships a first-class Temporal integration.

DBOS persists application data and execution state in Postgres or SQLite and runs in-process as a library with no new infrastructure; a DBOSAgent wrapper makes Pydantic AI agents durable, and it gives exactly-once execution via transactional semantics.

Inngest offers step.ai.infer (proxies long-running LLM requests to reduce serverless compute cost), step.ai.wrap (adds retries and telemetry to any AI SDK call) and AgentKit; it has a $20M Series A and production users include Day.ai and Browser Use.

Restate Cloud opened publicly in 2025 with usage-based pricing; production use cases include AI workflows, crypto trading and banking infrastructure, and it suits edge/serverless deployments better than Temporal.
Microsoft's Azure Durable Task Extension (public preview, late 2025) supports multi-day human-in-the-loop pauses, scale-to-zero and orchestration versioning for the Microsoft Agent Framework.

Journal-based replay (Temporal, Restate) re-executes the workflow function from the start, returns cached results for steps already in the journal, and continues from the first unjournaled step; it requires deterministic workflows, so LLM calls must be wrapped as activity steps.

Naive retry of a 12-step pipeline that crashes at step 10 restarts from step 1, repeating pay-per-use API calls; LLM tool calls like book_flight() are not naturally idempotent, so a second call produces a second booking.
Inngest's human-in-the-loop pattern maps to durable execution's suspend/resume primitives, letting workflows pause for hours or days awaiting approval without losing state.
Compounding reliability: five steps at 99% each give about 95% overall success, and ten steps about 90%.

Restate assigns each virtual object a unique key (e.g. a session ID), serializes handler calls on it, and journals each ctx.run() before execution, giving exactly-once semantics without application-level idempotency keys.
Inngest checkpoints each step.run() output; on failure it re-invokes the function and returns cached results for completed steps.

In Temporal, GPU-bound or side-effecting operations (vLLM inference, fine-tuning, embeddings) should go in activities, not workflow code, because workflow code must be deterministic and replays on every worker restart.
Temporal workflow history is capped at 50,000 events or 50 MB, so long-running reasoning loops should call workflow.continue_as_new() to archive history and reset the event log.
Inngest's step primitives are step.run(), step.sleep(), step.waitForEvent() and step.invoke(); each step boundary costs an HTTP roundtrip, adding roughly 15 ms to 50 ms of dispatch overhead per step.

Temporal Cloud enforces a 2 MB per-payload limit, a 4 MB event-history transaction limit, and 51,200 events / 50 MB history cap; the suggested workaround is the claim-check pattern of storing payloads in S3 and passing a reference through history.

Temporal shipped a first-party OpenAI Agents SDK integration in April 2026 with an activity_as_tool helper that turns Activities into OpenAI-compatible tool schemas, so tool calls become durable Activities and the loop is a Workflow; Stripe, Snap and Coinbase are named as Temporal users.
